'''Maria-Elisabeth Michel-Beyerle''' (born 20 August 1935 in [[Kiel]], [[Germany]]) is a German chemist. From 1974 to 2000, she was a professor of Physical Chemistry at the [[Technical University of Munich]]. Among other awards, she has received the 2000 [[Bavarian Order of Merit]] (Bayerischer Verdienstorden), the highest service order bestowed by the Free State of Bavaria, for her work on [[photosynthesis]].

== Early life ==
On 20 August 1935 Michel-Beyerle was born in [[Kiel]], Germany. Michel-Beyerle's father was [[Konrad Beyerle]], an engineer.{{Citation needed|date=March 2022}}

==Education and career==
Michel-Beyerle studied chemistry at the [[University of Göttingen]]. From 1957 to 1959, she studied at the [[Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München]]. From 1960 to 1962, she was a graduate assistant at the Institute of Inorganic Chemistry at [[RWTH Aachen University]].<ref name=TechnischeBio/> In 1964, she completed her doctoral thesis, ''Zur Elektrochemie des Indiums'', on the electrochemistry of [[indium]].<ref name=Emeriti>{{cite web|title=Maria-Elisabeth Michel-Beyerle (German)|url=http://www.emeriti-of-excellence.tum.de/index.php?id=69|website=Technische Universität München|access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref>

From 1965 to 1974, Michel-Beyerle worked as a research assistant at the Institute of Physical Chemistry at the [[Technical University of Munich]], working with [[Heinz Gerischer]].<ref name=Emeriti/><ref name=TUM/> In 1974 she achieved her [[Habilitation]], qualifying as a professor and being appointed to the Chair of Physical Chemistry at the Technical University of Munich. In 1980, she was recognized as a  [[Academic ranks in Germany|Professor extraordinarius]]. Michel-Beyerle became a [[Professor emeritus]] in 2000.<ref name=Emeriti/>

She has been the founder and spokesperson for two Collaborative Research Centres, one for  “Elementary processes of photosynthesis” (1981–1996) and one for “Photoionisation and charge transfer in large molecules, clusters and in the condensation phase“ (1994–2000).<ref name=TechnischeBio/> From 2003 to 2007, she has been the project coordinator of the EU research program for "Control of assembly and charge transport dynamics of immobilized DNA" (CIDNA).<ref name=Emeriti/><ref name=CIDNA>{{cite web|title=Home|url=http://csbiochem.de/|website=Control of assembly and charge transport dynamics of immobilized DNA|access-date=2016-01-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160111233841/http://csbiochem.de/|archive-date=2016-01-11|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In 2008, she became a visiting professor at [[Nanyang Technological University]] in the city state of  [[Singapore]].<ref name=TechnischeBio/> In 2009, she became the founding director of BioFemtoLab, a research unit at Nanyang Technological University.<ref name=Oceanian>{{cite web|title=Regional Focus – APA Singapore|url=https://www.a-star.edu.sg/Portals/59/images/IMU/newspapers/APA-Newsletter-April-2012.pdf|website=Newsletter April 2012|publisher=The Asian and Oceanian Photochemistry Association|access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref><ref name=Nanyang>{{cite web|title=Prof Maria-Elisabeth Michel-Beyerle|url=http://research.ntu.edu.sg/expertise/academicprofile/Pages/StaffProfile.aspx?ST_EMAILID=MARIAELISABETH|website=Nanyang Technological University|access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref>

==Research==
Michel-Beyerle's area of research is [[physical chemistry]].  She is known for her work on electron transfer dynamics in biological systems, including the influence of magnetic fields on chemical reactions such as the spin dynamics of radicals, and the use of MARY-spectroscopy (Magnetic Field Effect on Reaction Yield)<ref name=Atherton>{{cite book|last1=Atherton|first1=N. M.|last2=Davies|first2=M.J.|last3=Gilbert|first3=B.C.|title=Electron Paramagnetic Resonance: A review of the recent literature to 1997|date=1998|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|location=Cambridge, UK|isbn=978-0-85404-305-7|page=259|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=l7XBH2nntjkC&pg=PA259|access-date=13 January 2016|ref=Atherton}}</ref> to study structural and dynamic properties of the reaction centre.<ref name=Bube>{{cite journal|last1=Bube|first1=W.|last2=Haberkorn|first2=R.|last3=Michel-Beyerle|first3=M. E.|title=Magnetic field and isotope effects induced by hyperfine interaction in a steady state photochemical experiment|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|date=September 1978|volume=100|issue=19|pages=5993–5995|doi=10.1021/ja00487a002}}</ref><ref name=Lersch>{{cite journal|last1=Lersch|first1=W.|last2=Michel-Beyerle|first2=M.E.|title=Magnetic field effects on the recombination of radical ions in reaction centers of photosynthetic bacteria|journal=Chemical Physics|date=July 1983|volume=78|issue=1|pages=115–126|doi=10.1016/0301-0104(83)87012-8|bibcode=1983CP.....78..115L}}</ref> She has examined the structure of the [[photosynthetic reaction center]]  in bacteria.<ref name=RCP2012>{{cite book|editor-last1=Michel-Beyerle|editor-first1=Maria-Elisabeth|title=The Reaction center of photosynthetic bacteria : structure and dynamics|date=2012|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|location=[S.l.]|isbn=978-3-642-64723-9}}</ref><ref name="Govindjee">{{cite book |last1=Govindjee |first1=J. Thomas Beatty |last2=Gest |first2=H. |last3=Allen |first3=J.F. |title=Discoveries in Photosynthesis |date=2005 |publisher=Springer |location=Netherlands |isbn=978-1-4020-3323-0 |page=219 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=I3gy4r-aBusC&pg=PA219 |access-date=8 January 2016}}</ref> Her work with [[Johann Deisenhofer]] and [[Hartmut Michel]] informed their understanding of unidirectional electron transfer, contributing to their winning of the Nobel Prize in chemistry for determining the three-dimensional structure of the photosynthetic reaction center.<ref name=Nobel>{{cite web|last1=Deisenhofer|first1=J.|last2=Michel|first2=H.|title=Nobel lecture. The photosynthetic reaction centre from the purple bacterium Rhodopseudomonas viridis|url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/chemistry/laureates/1988/deisenhofer-michel-lecture.pdf|website=Nobel Prize.org|date=December 8, 1988}}</ref><ref name=Plato>{{cite journal|last1=Michel-Beyerle|first1=M. E.|last2=Plato|first2=M.|last3=Deisenhofer|first3=J.|last4=Michel|first4=H.|last5=Bixon|first5=M.|last6=Jortner|first6=J.|title=Unidirectionality of charge separation in reaction centers of photosynthetic bacteria|journal=Biochimica et Biophysica Acta (BBA) - Bioenergetics|date=January 20, 1988|volume=932|issue=1|pages=52–70|doi=10.1016/0005-2728(88)90139-9}}</ref> She is particularly interested in disorder phenomena and the control of disorder-order transitions.<ref name=Professor>{{cite web|title=MICHEL- BEYERLE, Maria-Elisabeth Professor|url=http://www.spms.ntu.edu.sg/PAP/Home/Faculty/Michel_Beyerle.html|website=Nanyang Technological University|access-date=13 January 2016}}</ref> She was the first to identify very rapid transmembrane electron transfers and examine their energetics.<ref name=TechnischeBio>{{cite web|title=Maria-Elisabeth Michel-Beyerle (English)|url=http://www.emeriti-of-excellence.tum.de/en/portraits/maria-elisabeth-michel-beyerle/|website=Technische Universität München|access-date=12 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160629140114/http://www.emeriti-of-excellence.tum.de/en/portraits/maria-elisabeth-michel-beyerle/|archive-date=29 June 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref and proteins include the [[green fluorescent protein]] (GFP) of the [[jellyfish]] [[Aequorea victoria]].<ref name=Nanyang/><ref name=Jung>{{cite ==Honors and awards==
* 2000,  [[Bavarian Order of Merit]] (Bayerischer Verdienstorden), highest service order bestowed by the Free State of Bavaria<ref name=Verdienstorden>{{cite web|title=Search for Maria-Elisabeth Michel-Beyerle|url=http://www.bayerischer-verdienstorden.de/cda/presentation/index.php|website=Bayerischer Verdienstorden|access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref>
* 2006,  [[Bavarian Maximilian Order for Science and Art]] (Bayerischer Maximiliansorden für Wissenschaft und Kunst), for those "who have set new standards with their lifetime achievement in science and art".<ref name=Heinrichsen>{{cite web|last1=Heinrichsen|first1=Dieter|title=Höchste Auszeichnung für TU-Chemikerin: Maria Elisabeth Michel-Beyerle erhält Maximiliansorden|url=https://idw-online.de/de/news143790?print=1&id=143790|website=IDW Informationsdienst Wissenschaft|date=January 20, 2006}}</ref>
* 2009, Bavarian Constitutional Medal, ([[Bayerische Verfassungsmedaille]]), Silver<ref name=MEMIM>{{cite web|title=Bayerische Verfassungsmedaille|url=http://memim.com/bayerische-verfassungsmedaille.html|website=MEMIM Encyclopedia|access-date=11 January 2016|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304085146/http://memim.com/bayerische-verfassungsmedaille.html|archive-date=4 March 2016}}</ref>
* 2013, Heinz Maier-Leibnitz-Medaille from the Technical University of Munich<ref name=TechnischeBio/><ref name=Heinz>{{cite web|title=Heinz Maier-Leibnitz-Medaille|url=https://portal.mytum.de/tum/honoratioren/HML/index_html|website=Technische Universität München|access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref>
